_comment: How readiness and thesis fit are judged, editable without code. Ladders are cumulative: a company is at level N only when every rung up to N is answered 'yes' with a quoted source. The first rung that isn't is the blocker. Answers live in each company's evidence.checklist ({'business.6': {answer, quote, url, source, by}}); the engine (app/engine.py ladder) turns them into a level. A level with no answers falls back to the 0-5 evidence factors in weights.json.

sources._comment: How much a source is worth, best first. A 'yes' from 'ai' (a model's inference with no quote found in the sources) never counts towards a ladder, and an investment factor backed only by 'ai' is down-weighted and capped.

tech.label: Tech readiness (TRL)
tech.framework: Technology Readiness Level 1-9 (Aalto University / EU Horizon definitions)

rungs.title: Basic principles observed
rungs.question: Are the basic scientific principles behind the technology observed and reported?

rungs.title: Technology concept formulated
rungs.question: Is the technology concept or application formulated (designed, even if not built)?

rungs.title: Experimental proof of concept
rungs.question: Has an experimental proof of concept been shown?

rungs.title: Validated in the lab
rungs.question: Has the technology been validated in a lab?

rungs.title: Validated in a relevant environment
rungs.question: Has it been validated in a relevant environment (realistic conditions)?
rungs.blocker: not validated in a relevant environment

rungs.title: Demonstrated in a relevant environment
rungs.question: Has a prototype been demonstrated in a relevant environment, e.g. a field pilot or trial?

rungs.title: Prototype in operational environment
rungs.question: Has a system prototype run in an operational environment with real users?

rungs.title: System complete and qualified
rungs.question: Is the system complete and qualified, in use by paying customers?
rungs.blocker: system not complete or in customer use

rungs.title: Proven in operation
rungs.question: Is the actual system proven in operation, sold at scale?

business.label: Business readiness (BRL)
business.framework: KTH Innovation Readiness Level: Business Readiness Level 1-9

rungs.title: Business idea hypothesised
rungs.question: Is there a hypothesis of a possible business concept?

rungs.title: Concept described
rungs.question: Is the business concept described in a structured form (e.g. NABC), with the overall market and some competitors or alternatives identified?
rungs.blocker: concept, market or competitors not described

rungs.title: Draft business model
rungs.question: Is there a draft business model (canvas) with the market quantified (TAM/SAM) and a full competitor overview?
rungs.blocker: no business model draft or quantified market

rungs.title: Full business model
rungs.question: Is there a full business model including revenues and costs, with first economic projections?
rungs.blocker: no full business model with revenues and costs

rungs.title: Tested on the market
rungs.question: Have parts of the business model been tested with customers, with pricing hypotheses and differentiation verified by market feedback?
rungs.blocker: business model not tested with customers

rungs.title: Test sales
rungs.question: Is the full business model, including pricing, verified on customers by test sales (e.g. a paying pilot)?

rungs.title: Product/market fit
rungs.question: Is there product/market fit: significant customer use and sales where customers show clear payment willingness?

rungs.title: Model holds and can scale
rungs.question: Do sales and metrics show the business model holds and can scale, with sales channels and supply chain in place?
rungs.blocker: sales don't yet show the model holds

rungs.title: Scaling, profitable
rungs.question: Is the business scaling with growing recurring revenue, profitably?
rungs.blocker: not yet scaling with recurring revenue

ocean_impact.label: Ocean impact (Navigator KPI maturity)
ocean_impact.framework: Ocean Impact Navigator (1000 Ocean Startups): a KPI framework with no official levels. This is our 5-step measurement-maturity ladder over its impact areas and KPIs, not an official OIN level.
ocean_impact._impact_areas_source: WEF / 1000 Ocean Startups, The Ocean Impact Navigator (2023): '30 KPIs in six main impact areas'.

rungs.title: Ocean problem named
rungs.question: Does it name a specific ocean-health problem it tackles?

rungs.title: Mapped to a Navigator impact area
rungs.question: Does its impact clearly fall in one of the Navigator's impact areas (name it)?
rungs.blocker: not mapped to a Navigator impact area

rungs.title: KPI and baseline
rungs.question: Has it chosen an impact KPI and measured a baseline?

rungs.title: Measured in operation
rungs.question: Does it report that KPI over time from a pilot or real operations?

rungs.title: Independently verified
rungs.question: Is the impact independently verified (peer-reviewed study or third party)?

investment._comment: Redstone's investment-potential factors from the challenge brief, scored 0-5. The anchors say what a 1, 3 and 5 look like; every score needs a supporting quote and source (evidence.support).

market.label: Market
market.def: size and growth of its market, as an investor sees it.

anchors.1: niche or shrinking market, no sizing
anchors.5: large, fast-growing market with evidence of demand

product.label: Product
product.def: how mature and good the product is.

anchors.5: polished product in paying customers' hands

team.label: Team
team.def: strength and track record of the team, only if the sources describe it.

anchors.3: complete founding team with relevant experience
anchors.5: proven founders with prior exits or deep domain track record

business_model.label: Business model
business_model.def: how attractive the business model is to an investor (margins, recurring revenue).

anchors.1: no clear way to make money
anchors.5: recurring revenue with proven, attractive margins

marketing.label: Marketing & distribution
marketing.def: how credible its route to customers is (sales, partners, distribution).

anchors.3: first revenue or a funded round
anchors.5: strong revenue growth or well funded

tech.label: Tech
tech.def: technical depth and how hard it is to copy.

deal_dynamics.label: Deal dynamics
deal_dynamics.def: how attractive investing now is (round momentum, investor interest, terms).

anchors.1: ask out of line with traction

impact.label: Impact
impact.def: ocean impact as part of the investment case.

anchors.1: impact claimed, not part of the case
anchors.3: impact plausible and linked to revenue
anchors.5: impact central to the case and evidenced

theses._comment: Thesis fit per holder: hard gates first (out of scope = no fit, with the reason), then a stage window (fit peaks in a band and falls off outside it), then the weighted evidence factors. Every criterion here is an EDITABLE DEFAULT, not the partners' real thesis: replace them with what A'Pelago and Redstone say (Admin > Thesis criteria, or edit this file). countries: '*' or a list of countries and regions (Nordic, EU, Baltic). ticket_eur: [min, max] in euros, either may be null; null switches the gate off. sectors: words matched against the sector and pitch (words of 5+ letters also match as a prefix: 'coast' finds 'coastal'); '*' accepts any.

apelago.label: A'Pelago accelerator
apelago.description: Early-stage blue-economy accelerator: ocean impact, business readiness, founding team.
apelago.criteria_note: Editable default. Stage band and geography are placeholders until A'Pelago confirms its real criteria.

redstone.label: Redstone investment
redstone.description: Early-stage venture: market, product, team, business model, financials, deal dynamics.
redstone.criteria_note: Editable default. Ticket size and geography are off until Redstone confirms its real criteria.
